title: Markets drop ahead of Nvidia’s results; Jensen Huang says he’d be ‘honoured’ to return as CEO – as it happened
text:
Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news

 Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return to Nvidia as CEO 

 Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war 

 China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers. 

 At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:

 “The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s high-tech industries.”

 “This is the worst situation possible for China because the last thing they want to see is any new restrictions on their access to chips.”

 “Export controls are what upset them practically more than anything else right now other than maybe Taiwan.”

 Deutsche plotted an expansion of its notorious Russia business under chief executive Christian Sewing, over-ruling the fears of its compliance team about the bank’s Kremlin-connected clientele as geopolitical storm clouds gathered.

 The bank accidentally leaked Trump’s tax statements during his first presidential term and kept the mistake secret from the White House, with Sewing briefed on its handling of the crisis.

 Deutsche processed almost $600mn of suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein , a far higher figure than previously known.

 A catalogue of compliance deficiencies, governance weaknesses, ineptitude and technology failings, including a confession to regulators that Deutsche was in effect “operating outside of law and order”.
